newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Siemens to join Sofia airport project.
newsitem.headline: Siemens to join Sofia airport project.

text.p: Germany's Siemens AG is expected to acquire a majority stake in a new venture to modernise Sofia airport, Bulgarian officials said on Wednesday.
They said the agenda of the venture's shareholders meeting on Thursday envisaged raising the company's capital to 114 million levs ($62,700) from 56 million levs.
"The meeting is expected then to decide whether Siemens will acquire a 51 percent stake worth 58 million levs," said an official from Sofia City Council who declined to be named.

She said apart from Siemens and the airport, the Sofia City Council would hold a share in the venture after buying a 17 percent stake worth 9.5 million levs from Bulgarian construction company Glavbolgarstroy.

Transport ministry officials said financing of the 56-year-old airport's reconstruction had been almost ensured as Bulgaria expected the European Investment Bank's board to approve a loan worth 60 million Ecu ($64.8 mlillion).

"Another 25 million Ecu will come from the European Union's Phare programme. We also expect negotiations with the Kuwaiti Development Fund for an initial loan worth $40 million for the project," transport ministry spokeswoman Valya Luleva told Reuters.
President Petar Stoyanov said last month after a visit to Kuwait that there was a possibility for more credits later from the Fund.

The first stage of the reconstruction, which includes enlargement of a passenger terminal to handle 3.5 million passengers per year and lengthening the runway, is expected to cost some $120 million. Another $20-25 million will be needed for a cargo terminal to handle up to 60,000 tonnes per year.
Ahead of the airport venture's meeting, the transport minister appointed on Wednesday a new board of directors for Sofia Airport, Luleva said.

The new board has elected as its chairman current deputy transport minister Petko Tabakov, replacing Stanislav Velinov. The board also elected Zdravko Velichkov, former director of the state Hemus Air airline, as the Sofia Airport executive director replacing Danyo Adanev. -- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145 ($ = 1817 Bulgarian Levs)
